relevance_note: The paper gives individual-level dried-bloodspot GHB data for patients with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency ('GHB determinations in DBS of nine SSADHD patients (eight 1^st screens, four 2^nd screens) revealed a range of 111–767 μM (median, 388)'), so identifiable in-scope persons are described, although no ALDH5A1 variant description is printed.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules; no script was used and Table 1 was transcribed by hand. The paper prints no variant description for any person (confirmation is described only as 'ALDH5A1 molecular analyses' and 'data not shown'), so every variants row keeps variant_original_string 'not reported' (v3, D-22), with the gene tie taken from the confirmation sentence. Individuals: the 19 post-newborn patients of Table 1 (one table row = one patient; Fig. 2A: 'all nineteen patients characterized'), labelled 'Table 1 row <k>' (k counting data rows from the top), plus the previously published patient of ref [10], labelled 'ref [10] patient' (text rule 4; the label 'Table 1 row 5' is already used for the fifth post-newborn row). The nine patients who contributed the 12 newborn dried bloodspots are described only as a group (counts with no individual mapping), so they got no rows; there is no single stated total (19 post-newborn and 9 newborn patients, at least two in both sets: the 8.7-year-old female and the 6.8-year-old male of the sibship). Table 1's post-newborn and newborn columns are not aligned by patient (the sibship male's 1st-screen value 226 μM is in row 1 while his own post-newborn row is row 7), so no newborn-column value was assigned by position (v6, D-31); only values the text names for a person were used (female 111 μM; male 226 and 116 μM). Table ages are ages at dried-bloodspot collection and were recorded as age at last evaluation. Sex is stated only for those two sibship members; the 11M/8F split is a group count. Age at onset and age at diagnosis are not given for any individual. The introduction's phenotype ('global delays, hypotonia, absence of speech and variable epilepsy') describes the disease, not these individuals, so all 20 checklist items are 'not reported' for everyone. Each patient's GHB concentration is recorded in phenotypic_features as the paper's metabolic hallmark (abstract: 'Increased gamma-hydroxybutyric acid in urine and blood'), with the person's own table value; for the nine post-newborn patients below the 78 μM newborn cutoff the status rests on the group statement about those nine ('For these patients (n=9)'). For the previously published patient, sex is not reported in this paper (the citation of ref [10] says 'female', but that is the reference text, not a statement about this patient) and Rett syndrome is recorded as an observed feature. Contradictions: none found. Other notes: the abstract says 'twelve archival newborn patient dried bloodspots' while the text says nine patients/12 DBS; 'Nineteen teen samples' appears to mean nineteen post-newborn samples; negative booleans (is_proband false) carry no span because the paper does not state them.

study_type.span: Archival newborn DBS were obtained with parental consent from nine patients (12 unique DBS) obtained from California, Texas, Maryland, and Ireland.

n_patients_reported.span: The figure shows the DBS GHB content for all nineteen patients characterized.

cites_prior_report_of_same_patients.span: Confirmation of SSADHD for patients contributing post-newborn DBS was previously confirmed through a combination of GHB measurement, ALDH5A1 molecular analyses, and assay of SSADH in white cells for older patients (data not shown) [7–9].
